title: SubmitOrchestrationRequest
description: Request body for POST /api/orchestration/submit. Sent by zekt-action v3 (orchestrate: true) on behalf of the consumer workflow. Each step targets a Zekt service by its immutable service_slug — the human-readable service name is never used for resolution or routing.

workflow_run_id.description: GitHub workflow run ID of the consumer workflow that is initiating this orchestration.

execution_mode.description: Execution strategy. 'sequential' dispatches each step after the previous one completes. 'parallel' dispatches every step whose dependencies are satisfied as soon as they are satisfied, following the depends_on graph.

default_service_owner.description: Optional convenience field: default GitHub org name used to resolve each step's target service when the step omits its own service_owner_name. Reduces boilerplate for chains where every step targets services owned by the same organization.

strict_output_schema_resolution.description: Spec 115. When true, a $zekt{{ steps.X.outputs.Y }} reference fails the referencing step at dispatch time if Y is not declared in service X's published step-output schema — even when Y is present in that run's actual output. When false or absent, resolution is unchanged: a reference resolves from the actual output and fails only if the field is genuinely missing. A step whose target service publishes no step-output schema is unaffected either way, so enabling this does not require every service in the chain to have declared its outputs. Chosen per run by the requestor: it is never inferred from a service, never enabled by default, and is read fresh on each template resolution.
strict_output_schema_resolution.$comment: Independent of the per-service SchemaEnforcementEnabled flag, which governs INPUT validation at dispatch. Conflating the two would tie a requestor's template policy to a provider's input policy.

services.description: Ordered list of service steps to orchestrate. In sequential mode, each step runs after the previous one completes successfully.

OrchestrationStep.description: One step in the orchestration chain. The (service_owner_name, service_slug) tuple uniquely resolves to either a provider ServiceDescription or a consumer ConsumerServiceDescription (SubscriberFires direction only). Consumer services with EventDirection: OwnerFires cannot be orchestration targets.

step_id.description: Consumer-assigned identifier for this step. Must be unique within the request. Used in depends_on references and in $zekt{{ steps.STEP_ID.outputs.FIELD }} template expressions in later steps. Never uses the service_slug — this is a caller-defined logical name.

service_slug.description: The immutable, machine-readable identifier of the Zekt service to invoke. Set by the service owner in the Zekt Registry, unique per owner. This is the ONLY field used to resolve the target — the human-readable name is never used for routing.

service_owner_name.description: GitHub organization name of the service owner. Combined with service_slug to resolve the target service. May be omitted per-step when default_service_owner is set at the request level; a step-level value overrides the default. Not a secret — GitHub org names are already public.

requested_by.description: Human-readable identifier for the requesting team. Informational only — never used for authorization, routing, or resolution.

depends_on.description: step_id values that must reach 'completed' status before this step is dispatched. In sequential mode, Zekt auto-populates this as [previous_step_id] if omitted, so it can be left empty for linear pipelines.

condition.description: Spec 162. Whether this step is part of the execution at all. Absent means the step is included and the plan behaves exactly as it did before conditions existed. true includes the step; false excludes it, along with every step that depends on it — transitively, through either a depends_on entry or a $zekt{{ steps.X.outputs.Y }} reference to it. An excluded step is never dispatched, holds no approval gate, costs nothing, and is not a failure: an execution whose steps are all completed or excluded ends 'completed'. Must be a JSON boolean; a string, a number or null is refused with an error naming the step.
condition.$comment: Never evaluated by Zekt. The value is a GitHub expression the consumer's runner has already evaluated, which is why it must arrive as a literal boolean — write "condition": ${{ <expression> }} unquoted in the workflow. Zekt-side expressions, and conditions over another step's outputs, are deliberately out of scope: a value that does not exist until dispatch time cannot be decided at submit.

condition_description.description: Spec 162. Display-only text shown with the condition in the Zekt console and in zekt-action's job summary. Never evaluated and never acted on. Only allowed on a step that also carries 'condition' — a description of a condition that does not exist is a plan mistake, and is refused.

timeout_minutes.description: Maximum time this step may take, in minutes, before the orchestration treats it as timed out.

input_schema_version.description: Semantic version of the target service's input schema that this step's 'input' was written against.

input.description: Arbitrary input payload for this step. Passed verbatim to the target service workflow via repository_dispatch client_payload.input. String values may contain $zekt{{ steps.STEP_ID.outputs.FIELD }} template expressions; these are resolved by the Zekt backend at dispatch time after the referenced step has completed. Dot-notation paths are supported: $zekt{{ steps.STEP_ID.outputs.a.b.c }}. The $zekt prefix is required: a plain ${{ … }} is GitHub expression syntax, so the consumer's runner evaluates it before zekt-action reads the payload, and because a step id here names a Zekt step rather than a GitHub workflow step it resolves to an empty string, silently.
input.$comment: Max serialized size: 256 KB. Validated against the target service's registered schema (if any) at submission time (pre-template) and again at dispatch time (post-template).

examples.$comment: Verbose form — service_owner_name repeated on every step
Concise form — default_service_owner set once, steps inherit it, with spec 115 strict output references enabled
Mixed form — default set, but one step overrides for a different owner
